correctness.rationale: The presence-probability bijections yield an exact signed partition-number minor; strict p(m) log-concavity from DeSalvo--Pak for m>=26 proves monotonic propagation. The finite rectangle 0<=a<=25, 1<=r<s<=26-a has exactly 2925 exact integer tests; all 26 saturated diagonal caps are positive, and the only negative saturated off-diagonal case is a=0,r=1. Analytic strict growth of p(s+1)>p(s) handles that infinite boundary. The 11 exceptional triples, five zeros, 25 finite edge cases, and 2884 negative-covariance finite cases match the actual checker, and the analytic extension proves all sizes. A separate direct partition-object enumeration and 562475 exact signs were replayed; neither is substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The two fixed part-presence Bernoulli variables are natural objects in random integer partitions. Their universal dependence sign is not obvious: exceptional small-index failures coexist with strict negative dependence, while the very large complementary pair remains positively correlated forever. The exact list of eleven isolated positive triples, five ties and unique large-size positive family solves a natural complete classification with an explicit boundary at n=17 and a reproducible finite certificate, not an arbitrary numerical cutoff.
